name: Nextmint Forms
author: sabuhiy

sections.description:
Nextmint Forms is a drag-and-drop form builder that turns submissions into leads in Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next. Build a form, connect it to your Form Handler, and embed it on any page. Submissions go straight to Salesforce.

Nextmint Forms is an independent integration and is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, Salesforce.

A visual builder. Drag your fields onto the canvas and watch a live preview. It is built on WordPress’s own components, so it looks at home in wp-admin.

Secure. Forms block spam by default with a honeypot and rate limiting. Turn on Google reCAPTCHA or Cloudflare Turnstile when you want more.

Simple to run. One plugin, one zip, no dependencies. Install it, build a form, paste your Form Handler URL, and embed.

Features

  • Visual drag-and-drop builder with a live preview
  • Two ways to connect: Server-side (WordPress sends to your Form Action URL and adds the spam tools) or Client-side (Salesforce’s script sends from the browser and adds web tracking)
  • Optional submission log, off by default: keep each submission (stored encrypted) with CSV export, or leave it off and store nothing
  • Spam protection: honeypot and rate limiting on by default, plus optional Google reCAPTCHA (v2/v3) or Cloudflare Turnstile
  • Shortcode and block embedding
  • Five style presets and a full Customize panel (fonts, colors, spacing, corners) with a mobile and desktop preview
  • Map each field to its Marketing Cloud Next external field name
  • Accessible styles that look the same on any theme

External services

This plugin can connect to the services below. Nothing loads on the front end unless you turn it on.

  • Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next. In Server-side mode, submissions are sent from your server to the Form Action URL you set. In Client-side mode, Salesforce’s form and tracking script loads in the visitor’s browser to send the form and enable web tracking. Sent: the field values a visitor submits and a generated unique id. See Salesforce’s Terms of Service (https://www.salesforce.com/company/legal/agreements/) and Privacy (https://www.salesforce.com/company/legal/privacy/).
  • Google reCAPTCHA (only if you turn it on). Google’s script (https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js) loads in the visitor’s browser on pages that show the form and sends the visitor’s IP address and interaction signals to Google. The resulting token is then checked from your server against https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Cloudflare Turnstile (only if you turn it on). Cloudflare’s script (https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js) loads in the visitor’s browser on pages that show the form and sends the visitor’s IP address and interaction signals to Cloudflare. The resulting token is then checked from your server against https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify. Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/. Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

Privacy

By default Nextmint Forms stores nothing: submissions relay straight to Salesforce. If you enable the optional log (off by default), each submission is kept, stored encrypted at rest. The admin table shows a summary (a masked email plus metadata: time, form, event, HTTP status, error code), and an admin can export the full submissions as CSV or delete them any time. The log is removed when you delete the plugin.

Nextmint Forms is an independent integration and is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, Salesforce.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to wp-content/plugins/nextmint-forms, or install it from Plugins > Add New in wp-admin.
  2. Activate Nextmint Forms.
  3. Open Nextmint Forms > Add New and build a form.
  4. On the Connect tab, choose Server-side or Client-side and paste the values from your published Marketing Cloud Next Form Handler’s Code Snippet tab (Form Action URL, or Content Key plus Script Base URL).
  5. Set each field’s External name to match your Form Handler, publish, and embed the form with its shortcode or block.

The in-plugin Help page walks you through the Salesforce side, step by step.

Building from source

The visual builder ships as a compiled bundle in build/. The uncompiled source is included with the plugin in the src/ directory. To rebuild it:

npm ci && npm run build
sections.faq:
Does it include spam protection?

Yes. Every form has a honeypot turned on by default, plus rate limiting, so most bots are blocked and real visitors never have to solve anything. If you want more, turn on Google reCAPTCHA (v2 or v3) or Cloudflare Turnstile. All of it keeps working on cached sites.

What do I need on the Salesforce side?

A published Form Handler in Marketing Cloud Next. From its Code Snippet tab, copy the Form Action URL (for Server-side) or the Content Key and Script Base URL (for Client-side). The Help page walks through each step.

Do I need to write code?

No. Build forms visually, map each field to its Marketing Cloud Next external name, and embed with a shortcode or block.

Which fields are supported?

Text, email, phone, URL, number, date, paragraph, dropdown, radio, checkboxes, a consent checkbox, hidden (auto-filled) fields, plus heading and text-block layout elements.

Does it store my visitors’ data?

No, not by default. Submissions relay straight to Salesforce and nothing is written to your database. If you turn on logging (off by default), each submission is kept, stored encrypted, so you can export it as CSV. Anyone with admin access can then export or delete that data, so leave it off unless you need it.
sections.changelog:
0.1.0

  • Initial release: visual builder, Server-side and Client-side connection modes, optional masked log, spam protection (honeypot, rate limiting, optional CAPTCHA), renderer, shortcode, block, and admin screens.
